vue.name: Vue 3
vue.purpose: Reactive UI framework — declarative templates, reactive state, event handling
vue.usage: Global build. Mount with Vue.createApp(options).mount('#app'). Prefer the Composition API: const { createApp, ref, computed, onMounted } = Vue. No build step, no .vue files.

bootstrap.name: Bootstrap 5
bootstrap.purpose: Responsive UI components and grid system — buttons, cards, navbars, modals, forms
bootstrap.usage: Include BOTH the CSS link and the JS bundle. Use utility classes (d-flex, gap-2, p-3) and components (btn btn-primary, card, row/col-md-6). For modals/dropdowns use data-bs-toggle="modal" data-bs-target="#id" — no JS needed.
bootstrap.example: Hello

peerjs.name: PeerJS
peerjs.purpose: WebRTC 1:1 video / audio / data calls — P2P media, free public signaling server
peerjs.usage: Create a Peer() — it registers with the public PeerJS signaling server. Signaling goes through their WebSocket; AUDIO/VIDEO GO DIRECT (P2P, encrypted). Caller: peer.call(remoteId, localStream). Callee: peer.on('call', call => { call.answer(localStream); call.on('stream', s => remoteVideo.srcObject = s) }). Room ID in location.hash makes the share link literally location.href — no backend. getUserMedia requires HTTPS (GitHub Pages provides it).

chartjs.name: Chart.js
chartjs.purpose: Canvas charts — bar, line, pie, doughnut, radar, scatter
chartjs.usage: new Chart(canvasEl, { type, data: { labels, datasets }, options }). Canvas needs explicit width/height. Destroy existing chart instance before re-rendering (chart.destroy()).
chartjs.example:
<canvas id="chart" width="400" height="200"></canvas>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4.4.1/dist/chart.umd.min.js"></script>
<script>
  new Chart(document.getElementById('chart'), {
    type: 'bar',
    data: { labels: ['Mon','Tue','Wed'], datasets: [{ label: 'Hours', data: [3, 7, 5] }] }
  });
</script>

marked.name: marked
marked.purpose: Markdown to HTML — user-editable text, notes, docs
marked.usage: marked.parse(str) returns an HTML string. NEVER insert marked output directly into innerHTML for user-supplied text — always wrap with DOMPurify.sanitize().

dompurify.name: DOMPurify
dompurify.purpose: HTML sanitizer — strips XSS from any user-supplied markup (use with marked)
dompurify.usage: DOMPurify.sanitize(dirtyHtml) returns safe HTML. Required whenever you innerHTML something that came from a textarea, URL param, or user storage. Combine with marked for safe markdown.
